text:
Alex: ap-southeast-1 GPU cluster is degrading — ~30% of worker nodes in that AZ showing kernel panics / kube node not-ready. Serving queues are backing up and tail latency spiking. Investigating but going to shift traffic now to avoid SLA impact :rotating_light:
Ben: any immediate error logs? driver OOMs or disk issues?
Alex: kernel panic traces + node reboots. Some nodes stuck in ImagePullBackOff for our nvidia driver sidecar. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/apac-gpu-latency (watch the 99th perc). infra-bot posted node-reboot counts.
Carla: agree shift. Plan: slow weight migration from APAC -> US then EU. Canary 10% steps, 30s pause, monitor health. Also pre-warm KV/prefix cache in target regions to avoid huge token/regeneration cost.
SRE-Oncall: @Alex do the glb weight changes via control-plane cli; recommend pauses between each 10% step and bump healthcheck timeout to 10s during the drift so we don't flip for transient p50 jitter. Drain APAC connections as weights drop.
Alex: executing now. Commands I'm running:
```
# decrease APAC weight, increase US/EU
glbctl set-weight --region ap-southeast-1 --weight 10
glbctl set-weight --region us-west-2 --weight 70
glbctl set-weight --region eu-west-1 --weight 20
# check pool health
glbctl get-pool --region ap-southeast-1 --format json
```
deploy-bot: GLB config applied (req=glb-1742001110-01) — new weights propagated.
Ben: note this will route more traffic into us-west-2 dedicated pools; we should cap background batch/embeddings to avoid exhausting GPUs. Cost delta expected ~+12% if sustained.
Carla: throttling batch queues now:
```
batchctl set-rate --queue embeddings --rate 0.5 --region us-west-2
```
Alex: also kicking cache prewarm for top models to reduce cold-call regen cost:
```
cachectl prewarm --models gptx-2,gptx-3 --regions us-west-2,eu-west-1
```
infra-bot: autoscaler triggered: launched 4 x p4d-like nodes in us-west-2 (scaling group: redwood-dedicated-usw2-1), req=asg-7841.
SRE-Oncall: healthchecks for new paths look good. Latency 99p back to baseline in ~90s. Keep watch for 30m. Open an incident in incidents/ and create a postmortem ticket for driver image rollout.
Alex: created incidents/1742001110 in channel incidents, assigned to @Carla for postmortem. Also opening a ticket with cloud provider for the kernel panic nodes.
Ben: reminder — Dedicated customers in APAC may have had degraded performance. We should notify sales/support to contact impacted customers and offer capacity credits if SLA breached.
Carla: I'll coordinate comms with CS and include rollback plan if APAC comes back noisy. We'll also schedule a rolling reprovision of affected nodes with updated driver image.
Alex: final status: weights stable (APAC 10 / US 70 / EU 20). Draining APAC, autoscaled US, batch throttled, cache prewarm started. Monitoring window 30m, will update thread.
Ben: :thumbsup:
SRE-Oncall: great work. Postmortem next steps: timeline, root cause, driver image QA gaps, and GLB canary improvements.
Alex: noted. Assigning follow-ups to infra tickets. Thanks everyone.
